_meta.note: Industry, peers, street, ownership, stock, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts for the Gland Pharma initiation. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026.

iqvia.item: Global medicines market to grow 5-8% a year to ~US$2.4 tn (invoice prices) by 2029; generics and biosimilars partly offset spending growth
iqvia.src: IQVIA, quoted in Gland AR FY26 MD&A

genericInjectables.src: Industry estimate quoted in Gland AR FY26 MD&A

complexTam.item: US TAM of Gland's 24 complex injectables (peptides US$1.65 bn, nano-suspension US$3.04 bn, hormones US$0.69 bn, microspheres US$0.71 bn)

pricing.item: US generic injectables: FY25 volume +9%, price -5% for Gland (CEO, 20-May-2025); the US market grows ~3-4% a year (Srinivas Sadu, 10-Aug-2026); Gland wins share through GPO contracts on a lower cost base

tariffs.item: US confirmed it will not impose Section 232 tariffs on generic pharmaceuticals (Q2FY26 call, Nov-2025); tariffs from 2026 target patented drugs and their APIs. Gland makes no patented products today (CFO/Chairman, 10-Aug-2026); CDMO partners in Europe and the US may move branded supply to the US, which can cut either way

chinaPlusOne.item: Big pharma's sterile manufacturing in Europe costs 5-6x India; companies source from 80-100 sites and want fewer, cheaper partners (Srinivas Sadu, 10-Aug-2026). The BIOSECURE Act (US) restricts certain Chinese biotech suppliers; Gland's Chinese parent is a disclosure point for US partners, though Gland's plants are in India and Europe

glp1.item: Semaglutide and liraglutide generics open market by market (Canada, India, Brazil and others from 2026; the US around 2031-32); fill-finish capacity for pens/cartridges is scarce; Gland raised cartridge capacity from 40 mn to 140 mn units and has 9 GLP-1 contracts, but expects meaningful US volumes only in FY30-31

westAsia.item: West Asia conflict: glass/vial suppliers asked for 5-6% price rises; 1-2% potential margin impact; Saudi shipments halted in Q4FY26 and NUPCO tender awards delayed

excluded.BIOCON: One-off and boom-bust EPS; P/E above 100x inside the window (PLAYBOOK 7c)

peers.notes: Pharma peer set set on 23-Nov-2026 (PLAYBOOK 7c). Gland is outside the nine-name set, so the five-year factor is the median of all nine: +8.2% P/E (+7.5% EV/EBITDA), as set for A21. Because Gland's base window starts at the Cenexi completion (27-Apr-2023), the factor applied is the nine peers' move against their own medians over that same window (+9.2% P/E, +5.1% EV/EBITDA), computed in tools/authoring/GLAND.ctx.js. Context peers: Aurobindo (Eugia injectables, Gland's closest listed rival in US generic injectables), Caplin Point (Caplin Steriles), and CDMOs (Syngene, Sai Life, Piramal Pharma, Laurus, Divi's); Biocon for biosimilars. moat.factor: Cost and scale in sterile manufacturing
moat.evidence: 1.7 bn units of capacity across all formats; wins GPO contracts on cost (FY25 volume +9%); base EBITDA margin 35-40%, far above most US generic injectables makers
No warning letter or import alert since USFDA approval of Dundigal in 2003; Visakhapatnam clean in Sep-2026; 342 approved ANDAs
389 ANDAs filed, 1,828 registrations; but much of the portfolio is mature molecules with price erosion
Long-term supply and profit-share deals; one customer was 13.5% of FY26 revenue and two were 24.7% of FY25; partners own the front end and can switch suppliers on re-filing
Six complex products launched; the big microsphere/liposome opportunities are post-FY29
46% of revenue incl. Cenexi; new 55-SKU and NDDS deals; but most CDMO work is tech transfer of generics, not innovator molecules ('we don't have any innovative products right now')
US generic injectables lose ~5% a year in price; tender markets (Saudi) are won and lost on price

critiques: Guidance credibility: medium-term growth was 'low-20s' (May-2025), cut to 15% (May-2026) and raised to ~20% (Aug-2026); Cenexi's breakeven and double-digit margin targets have slipped every year.

Cenexi has destroyed value so far: ~EUR230 mn EV, a ~EUR60 mn capex plan and three years of losses for a business that made EUR2 mn of EBITDA in Q1FY27; management admitted the thesis is 'taking longer than what we estimated'.
Investor on the Q4FY25 call; CFO Ravi Mitra (20-May-2025)
The Q4FY26-Q1FY27 margin jump owes much to a few launches (Dalbavancin, multivitamin) and the weak rupee; constant-currency growth was 15% vs 20% reported in Q1FY27.
IIFL (Rahul Jeewani) on the Q1FY27 call; GAM
Promoter overhang: Fosun sold 6% in Jun-2024 and 6% in Sep-2026 to fund its own buyback and debt reduction; it is now below 50%.
Customer concentration and the B2B model: partners own the front end; one customer was 13.5% of FY26 revenue.
At ~36x FY27E and ~30x FY28E EPS the stock already prices most of the 20% CAGR management only began guiding in August.
GLP-1 is a 2030 story for Gland: the 140 mn cartridge line will be filled partly with insulin until US semaglutide generics arrive.
gaps: Broker methods, ratings and EPS for Jefferies, Investec, Kotak, IIFL, Nirmal Bang, 360 ONE, ICICI Securities (institutional), Goldman Sachs and Ambit were not disclosed in the press sources we could access; full reports were not available.
Q1FY27 base-business vs Cenexi split is derived (base +24% per CFO); the company stopped publishing the split from Q1FY27.
Named holders at Jun-2026 (above 1%) not available; Mar-2026 annual-report list used.
Capacity utilisation by Indian site and the product-level revenue of Dalbavancin, multivitamin and the top 10 molecules are not disclosed.
Constant-currency growth for FY26 and Q4FY26 not disclosed (management declined on the Q4 call).
Profit-share and milestone income are given only as rough percentages on calls, not in rupees.
conflicts: ICICI Securities target: Business Today lists Rs2,825 (institutional) while the ICICI Direct retail note of 11-Aug-2026 sets Rs3,150 (33x FY28E); both shown as separate rows.

Fosun's 4-Sep-2026 sale: Free Press Journal reports 4.55% (75.05 lakh shares on BSE, Rs2,121.5 cr) while Fosun's filing reports 9.897 mn shares (6.0%) for ~Rs2,800 cr including open-market trades; we use the filing.
Nomura's 27.5x on FY28-29E average EPS implies average EPS of ~Rs121, above most of the street; reported by an aggregator, not seen in the original note.
BofA's 18-May-2026 price objective is reported as Rs1,868 (equal to the 15-May close); not used.
